source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry/company commentary tied to Divi's FY25 results describes Divi's as a direct beneficiary of the 'China+1' shift, with global pharma majors diversifying API/CDMO sourcing away from China amid geopolitical friction and trade tariff risk; Divi's signed a long-term manufacturing and supply agreement with a global pharma major for advanced intermediates and announced ~Rs 650-700 crore capacity expansion to secure customer supply and expand its custom-synthesis (CDMO) footprint, with custom synthesis mix rising and management citing diversification of geography/program pipelines as a growth driver (FY25 revenue +19%, EBITDA margin +209bps).

inr_exposure.evidence: ~88% of FY25 revenue was export-derived (Europe ~56% of total revenue, North America ~16% of total revenue), implying substantial foreign-currency (USD and EUR) revenue exposure, but no explicit USD-only revenue percentage or hedging policy was found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories was not among the 16 companies selected/approved under India's PLI scheme for Bulk Drugs (KSMs/Drug Intermediates/APIs) as reported publicly (approved firms include Sun Pharma, Aurobindo, Dr Reddy's, Lupin, Mylan, Cipla, Cadila, etc.); no disclosure found of Divi's receiving PLI incentives.

inr_exposure.evidence: Royal Enfield exports (~12.3% of FY25 turnover) span 80+ countries including SAARC, Latin America and Southeast Asia, implying some foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no explicit USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy disclosure was found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Eicher Motors Limited is listed among the ~20 OEMs approved under the Champion OEM Incentive component of India's PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry (covering Battery Electric and Hydrogen Fuel Cell Vehicles across segments). Per government/industry sources, disbursement of incentives to several approved companies (reportedly including Eicher) is expected to begin from FY27, suggesting no material PLI revenue benefit had yet been recognized as of the FY2024-25 annual report.

Emcure Pharmaceuticals was among the domestic pharma companies approved under Group B of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (Dept. of Pharmaceuticals approved-applicant list); no revenue % attributed to PLI-linked products was disclosed in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing found. Company MD (Sudhanshu Vats) has publicly described Pidilite's 'export component' as 'small'; exports exist (selective markets in Asia, Middle East, Africa via Pidilite International Pte and subsidiaries) but no diversification narrative or China+1 attribution was located.

rural.evidence: Rural/semi-urban markets described in management commentary as growing ~1.5x faster than urban markets and cited as a continuing growth driver (MD commentary tied to FY24-25 results); regional brand Haisha Paints noted gaining share in southern rural/semi-urban markets. No explicit % of total revenue from rural/semi-urban disclosed in sources reviewed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported to hold a large net cash position (~Rs 25.7bn cash vs ~Rs 1.4bn total debt per third-party data as of FY24-25), implying low overall rate sensitivity, but the floating-vs-fixed split of borrowings was not found disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Vinyl Acetate Monomer (VAM), a crude-oil derivative, is a key raw material; third-party analyst estimates (conflicting, ranging ~30-40% in some reports and higher in others) put VAM at a significant share of raw material costs, with crude price changes flowing through to VAM cost with an estimated 3-4 month lag. Pidilite's own precise disclosed % was not confirmed in sources reviewed (primary AR PDF was inaccessible due to network/egress restrictions in this environment).

inr_exposure.evidence: Export/international revenue described by management as a small component of overall sales; no specific USD revenue % or formal hedging policy statement was found in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Adhesives/specialty chemicals (Pidilite's core business) is not among India's notified PLI scheme sectors (e.g., electronics, pharma, auto components, textiles, white goods, solar, telecom, steel, food processing). No evidence found of Pidilite PLI participation.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India is described (third-party industry note) as having roughly 90% domestic / 10% export production, exporting to 30+ countries, with export/data-center-linked orders cited as a growth driver in a recent quarter (Electrification orders of Rs 1,776 crore in Q3 supported partly by export orders). Separately, sell-side/industry commentary (e.g., Motilal Oswal capital-goods notes) links broader India industrial order growth to China+1 supply-chain shifts and PLI-driven capex, but no confirmed direct statement in ABB India's own AR attributing its growth explicitly to China+1 was located.

rural.evidence: Not applicable / not disclosed — ABB India is a B2B industrial automation, electrification and motion equipment company with no rural consumer-market revenue disclosure.

govt_capex.evidence: Management (Q1 CY2026 earnings call) stated government capex 'has started picking up but has not yet gathered pace' and called it a defining factor for large system orders, which depend on capex executed directly by government, EPCs, or end users. Industry analysts estimate that 20-25% of India's incremental ~Rs 5-6 lakh crore power transmission & distribution capex (CY26-CY30) flows to electrification products (switchgear, transformers, protection relays, grid automation) of the type ABB sells, and ABB's order backlog (~Rs 10,000-11,000 crore) is substantially exposed to data-center and grid/infrastructure demand. No company-disclosed % of revenue directly tied to government capex was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not a materially disclosed exposure — ABB India's core inputs are metals (copper, steel, aluminum) and electronic components rather than crude-oil-linked/petrochemical raw materials. No crude-oil-linked raw material % disclosure found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: ABB Group's stated general policy (per ABB Group-level disclosures) is to hedge material currency exposures through offsetting transactions with third-party financial institutions; India-entity-specific hedging policy detail was not confirmed from the primary AR.
inr_exposure.evidence: Export production estimated at ~10% of ABB India's output (third-party industry note); explicit disclosed USD revenue % not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found that ABB India is itself a direct recipient/beneficiary of a PLI scheme. PLI schemes are referenced only as a macro demand tailwind for the broader Indian capital goods/industrial sector in analyst commentary, not as a direct company benefit.

rural.evidence: No explicit rural/semi-urban revenue % found. Brokerage commentary (not the AR itself) referenced a 'rural resurgence' aiding demand for the Popular segment in FY24, with management stating it did not expect a material direct impact on that segment; primary AR PDF (Diageo media site) could not be fetched in this environment to confirm any disclosed rural revenue split.

crude_exposure.evidence: Glass bottles and ENA (extra-neutral alcohol) are cited as the company's largest raw material cost items; FY24 commentary noted ~12-15% inflation in glass bottle costs compressing EBITDA margin (16.0% vs 16.3% YoY), and the company introduced 100% recycled PET packaging for select brands in FY2023-24. No explicit % of raw materials linked to crude oil/petrochemicals was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: United Spirits is an overwhelmingly India-domestic liquor business (McDowell's, Royal Challenge, Signature, Antiquity, etc.); no evidence of material USD-denominated revenue or a disclosed hedging policy was found in sources reviewed.

FY25 (year ended Mar-2025) consolidated revenue was Rs 54,543 crore; India formulations contributed ~33% (Rs 16,900 crore), US formulations ~30% (Rs 16,240 crore, US$1,921mn), Emerging Markets ~18% (US$1,114mn), and Rest of World ~14% (Rs 7,163 crore); Global Specialty sales (mostly US-billed, overlapping with the US segment) were US$1,216mn. Figures sourced from Sun Pharma's own FY25 results press release/IR materials, not read directly from the AR PDF (fetch blocked in this environment). No explicit total USD-denominated-revenue % or forex hedging policy statement was found in sources reviewed; the 30% figure reflects the US-segment revenue share only, a likely floor on true USD exposure given Global Specialty and part of EM/ROW sales are also USD-linked.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries appears on India's Dept. of Pharmaceuticals list of approved applicants under the PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (Category 1 - complex generics/high-value products), with manufacturing plants at Halol, Gujarat and Dadra approved for incentives. Specific revenue contribution or incentive amount attributable to Sun Pharma was not found in an AR excerpt or IR material during this research.

govt_capex.evidence: Medanta is empanelled under Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) and CGHS/ECHS government health schemes; analyst commentary notes government-scheme receivables have longer credit/recovery periods (~100+ days for Ayushman Bharat) versus private payers, but no % of revenue tied to government schemes/capex was disclosed in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/market commentary tied to NFIL's export-led CDMO and specialty chemicals business describes 'global supply chain diversification with rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment.' Three anchor customers (Bayer Crop Science, Corteva Agriscience, Fermion) grew from 63% of export revenue in FY24 to 80% in 1HFY26, and multi-year contracts with global agrochemical majors were cited as evidence of diversification-driven order wins. Could not confirm the company's own MD&A uses the explicit phrase 'China+1' (network access to the AR PDF and IR site was blocked), so this is graded moderate rather than strong.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is fluorspar, sourced partly via JV (Swarnim Gujarat Fluorspar Pvt Ltd, with GMDCL and Gujarat Fluorochemicals) rather than crude-oil derivatives; some agrochemical/pharma intermediates may involve petrochemical-derived feedstocks, but no disclosed % of raw materials linked to crude oil was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: 77% of revenue came from exports vs. 23% domestic (Q4FY25), with export/CDMO revenue concentrated among US/Europe-based agrochemical and pharma majors (Bayer Crop Science, Corteva Agriscience, Fermion), implying majority USD-denominated revenue. Specific hedging policy language was not found in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party summaries describe Garware as exporting to 75+ countries with ~60-65% of consolidated revenue from overseas markets, and FY24 growth driven by Aquaculture (Chile, Norway) and Geosynthetics. No explicit 'China+1' or supply-chain-diversification-away-from-China framing was found in available sources.

govt_capex.evidence: Geosynthetics segment (used in road/rail/dam infrastructure projects) was cited as an FY24 growth driver, but no % of revenue tied to government capex was disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials (HDPE, PP/polypropylene, polyester, nylon) are crude-oil derivatives per rating-agency and trade-press commentary; company reportedly passes on raw-material inflation to customers with roughly a one-quarter lag. No exact % of raw material cost that is crude-linked was disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Described in third-party commentary as relying on a natural hedge from imported raw materials plus 'a few hedging practices' to mitigate forex volatility; no formal policy percentage disclosed.
inr_exposure.evidence: ~60-65% of consolidated revenue is from international/export markets (multiple recent-year disclosures), implying material USD/foreign-currency exposure, but the exact USD-denominated revenue % was not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: A PLI scheme for technical textiles/MMF exists (₹10,683 cr outlay, min. investment thresholds of ₹100-300 cr), but no source found confirming Garware Technical Fibres as a selected beneficiary.

govt_capex.evidence: Management commentary (Q4 FY25 earnings call, per search summaries) stated 'India's demand continues to be supported by government-led infrastructure development, railway modernization, urbanization, manufacturing expansion, and increasing focus on domestic value addition,' cited as a foundation for growth across steel, stainless steel, aluminium and specialty alloys. No specific % of revenue tied to government capex was quantified.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is widely reported as 'almost debt free' with a debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 9.2% (FY24), suggesting limited rate-sensitive liability exposure overall, but no floating-vs-fixed borrowing split was disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are iron ore and coal (integrated 'ore to metal' steel/ferro-alloys producer); no crude-oil-linked raw material dependency was identified as material for this company.

inr_exposure.evidence: Approximately 20-21% of revenue is described as export-linked in recent investor commentary (aluminium foil, ferro-chrome/ferro-manganese, and steel products among export lines), which exposes the top line and margins to external price/FX shocks; no explicit USD-revenue % or hedging policy was disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Shyam Metalics Flat Products (group entity) was among the companies selected by the Steel Ministry under India's PLI scheme for specialty steel (₹6,322 cr scheme; 67 of 79 applicants shortlisted, ~₹42,500 cr aggregate investment potential). No revenue % attributable to the scheme was disclosed.

rural.evidence: Company disclosures/press describe a pan-India distribution network of 60,000+ retail outlets with emphasis on semi-urban and rural penetration (mass brands like Old Monk, 8PM, Magic Moments), but no explicit % of revenue from rural/semi-urban markets was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt reported at ~₹868 crore (Mar 2025) vs ~₹749 crore (Mar 2024); company previously redeemed FCCBs via external commercial borrowings. No floating-vs-fixed rate split found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are ENA, grain/molasses, and packaging (glass bottles, PET, cartons, labels). Industry/press commentary for FY24-25 notes glass bottle costs up ~12-20% and packaging costs up 30-40% amid crude oil price spikes, since PET/plastic packaging is petrochemical-derived. No specific % of raw material basket disclosed as crude-linked.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (~10% of revenue) are partly USD-denominated (incl. Gulf/Middle East, Africa, Asia-Pacific, airport retail channels), but no specific USD revenue % or hedging policy disclosure was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of PLI scheme participation; IMFL/spirits is not a PLI-covered sector in India.

china_plus_one.evidence: AR/company materials emphasize diversification across products, platforms, customers and geographies 'to reduce concentration risk' and build resilience, with manufacturing plants in India, China, Mexico and the USA and ~76% of revenue from international sales. Company became the first Indian auto component maker certified under India's Auto PLI scheme (hub wheel drive motor, e-2W/e-3W traction motors), consistent with India's positioning as an alternative sourcing hub for global OEMs. No explicit 'China+1' terminology was located in AR text via available sources, so this is scored moderate rather than strong.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary inputs are steel, aluminum, and forged/machined metal components rather than petrochemical feedstocks; no crude-oil-linked raw material % disclosure found.

inr_exposure.evidence: ~76% of revenue is international; a Dec-2024-period breakdown cites North America + Europe combined at ~66% of revenue with India at ~28% (a separate, possibly later-quarter data point cites India 50%/Europe 26%/North America 15%/Asia 9%, but that appears to be Q1 FY27 rather than FY24-25 full-year data, so it was not used). Implies substantial USD/EUR-denominated revenue, but no formal hedging policy or precise USD % was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first Indian automotive component manufacturer certified under the government's Auto PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme, with certifications covering a hub wheel drive motor for e-2-wheelers and traction motors for e-2W/e-3W vehicles (filed 7 applications total). Specific % of revenue attributable to PLI incentives not disclosed in available sources.

govt_capex.evidence: No company-specific % disclosure found. Sector-level context: Union Budget 2025-26 earmarked ~INR 2,541 crore for tourism infrastructure (50 flagship destinations, 'Heal in India', 'Meet in India' MICE push); IHCL commentary frames its ~INR 6,000-7,500 crore five-year capex and Tier 2/3 city expansion as aligned with this national tourism push, but no revenue-attribution percentage was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL is reported as largely debt-light: cash and bank balances of INR 2,179 crore and liquid investments of INR 899 crore as of March 31, 2025, with CARE Ratings noting no significant debt outside lease liabilities as of late 2025. No floating-vs-fixed rate borrowing mix percentage was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Overseas/international hotel portfolio generated approximately INR 1,512 crore in FY2024-25 against consolidated revenue of INR 8,565 crore (~17.6%), used here as a proxy for non-INR revenue exposure (not confirmed as strictly USD-denominated, so usd_revenue_pct left null). No specific hedging policy disclosure was located.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company has disclosed borrowings of roughly INR 815 crore across ~13 loans from SBI, Axis Bank and HDFC Bank (largest: INR 300 crore from Axis Bank, June 2022), but no floating-vs-fixed rate breakdown percentage was found in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY2024-25 segmental revenue: Domestic formulations ~INR 2,269 crore, International formulations ~INR 1,128 crore, CDMO ~INR 446 crore, API ~INR 76 crore (total ~INR 3,919-3,960 crore). International/export formulations business (~42% of revenue) includes US, branded generics exports, and Russia/CIS markets; Q4FY25 international formulations rose 6% YoY to INR 282 crore driven by growth in Russia and branded generics exports. Exact USD-denominated share and hedging policy were not found in available sources, so usd_revenue_pct left null.

china_plus_one.evidence: AR/MD&A notes NESCAFE as a key contributor to export growth, with NESCAFE Sunrise gaining traction in Singapore and Taiwan and its first-ever export to Canada, while NESCAFE Intenso roasted beans entered Maldives and Sri Lanka. Exports are ~4% of revenue (forex earned Rs 784.83 crore vs total revenue Rs 19,089 crore, FY25). No China+1 or supply-chain-diversification framing is used; growth is described as market expansion, not diversification-driven.

rural.evidence: Nestle's AR/MD&A discusses its 'RUrban' rural distribution strategy (200,000+ villages, 28,000+ rural distribution points) and strong Tier II-VI town growth. Third-party analyst commentary (not an AR disclosure) estimates rural India contributes ~25% of revenue, but since this is not a company-disclosed figure it is not used here.

crude_exposure.evidence: MD&A/press commentary flags packaging material and edible oil cost inflation, and specifically cites crude-oil-linked packaging costs rising amid geopolitical (Middle East) tensions, but no specific percentage of raw materials tied to crude/petrochemicals is disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company uses forward contracts and rupee invoicing to manage transaction exposure from imports, exports, license/royalty fees to Nestle S.A., and capex; treasury function centrally monitors FX exposure. No explicit USD revenue % disclosed (exports are only ~4% of sales).

pli_scheme.evidence: Nestle India received Government of India approval in December 2021 under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI), under the 'processed fruits & vegetables' category (per Nestle India special announcement/press release). No revenue percentage tied to PLI is disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Integrated Report 2024-25 discusses US-China trade tensions and the proposed Biosecure Act as prompting global pharma players to diversify suppliers and invest in regional manufacturing hubs, positioning Lupin's India-based manufacturing and CDMO operations, and its 'API Plus' business (built on process chemistry/fermentation expertise), as well-placed to serve global customers seeking 'secure and diversified API sources.' Report also cites India's CDMO market growing from USD 3.5 Bn to a projected USD 25 Bn over the next decade on China diversification. Framing is opportunity/positioning-oriented rather than an explicit statement that current revenue/order growth is already attributable to China+1 shifts.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Lupin discloses exposure to USD-INR, EUR-INR, and ZAR-INR currency fluctuations across 100+ markets; company deploys natural hedges and forex derivatives (forward contracts) with layered hedging strategies, with treasury operations actively monitoring exposures. No single consolidated 'USD revenue %' figure was found, though North America (US) alone is 38% of consolidated revenue and is predominantly USD-denominated, with additional USD exposure from API and other export sales.
inr_exposure.evidence: North America contributed 38% of FY2025 consolidated revenue (US sales ~Rs 8,395 crore, up 16% YoY); Other Developed Markets (11%) and Emerging Markets (11%) and API (5%) add further hard-currency exposure, but a single blended USD-revenue percentage is not explicitly stated in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin was approved as one of 9 domestic 'Group A' companies (alongside Sun Pharma, Cipla, Dr. Reddy's, Aurobindo, Cadila, Glenmark, Intas, Torrent) under India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals; reporting indicates Lupin (with Cipla) has used the scheme to enhance production capacities in cardiovascular, anti-infective, and diabetes therapeutic segments. No specific revenue percentage attributable to PLI incentives is disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Coforge discloses a 'Government, outside India' vertical (up ~29.9% YoY in FY25), which is foreign-government IT services revenue, not Indian government infrastructure/capex-linked revenue; no India govt-capex revenue percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company uses forex/cash-flow hedges on foreign-currency (largely USD, GBP, EUR) receivables; per Q4FY26 earnings-call commentary, from FY26 realized gains/losses on cash flow hedges are reported under other income (forex gain/loss) rather than adjusted directly to revenue, following a mark-to-market hedge loss of roughly INR 140-150 crore in an earlier period.
inr_exposure.evidence: No explicit AR-disclosed %-of-revenue-in-USD figure found; geography split (Americas ~54%, EMEA ~35%, India ~10%) implies dominant USD/GBP/EUR billing given India is exporter of IT services.

pli_scheme.evidence: Coforge is an IT services exporter; PLI (manufacturing-incentive) schemes are not applicable/disclosed for this business.

rural.evidence: FY2024-25 city-wise sales distribution reported as: Metro 23%, Town Class 1 27%, Town Class 2-6 28%, Rural 22% — i.e. combined Town Class 2-6 + Rural (semi-urban/rural markets) accounts for ~50% of domestic sales, reflecting Mankind's strong field-force/distribution reach into tier-2 to tier-6 towns and rural India.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company has issued debt securities (NCDs, Oct 2024) at fixed coupon rates (7.99%/7.97%); no specific floating-rate-liability percentage disclosure found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure found confirming Mankind Pharma (or a subsidiary) is an approved beneficiary under India's pharma/bulk-drug PLI schemes; company is predominantly a domestic formulations player rather than a listed PLI-approved API/KSM manufacturer.
